title: Dévissage des complexes ½ simpliciaux ∂ - parfaits et structures multiplicatives… (1975 ou 1976) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, read from this page and the neighbouring ones. The interpretation of P. and C^·. is inferred; the page itself does not define them.

- k is a commutative ring.
- P. is a k-linear category of bounded complexes of finite free k-modules.
- Σ. is the class of degreewise split short exact sequences in P.
- C^·. is a 'universal' cochain object in P.: a sequence C^0. → C^1. → C^2. → … of complexes. It is presumably double-struck in the manuscript.

The statement under proof is on the previous page:
- (a) Restriction F ↦ F(C^·.) is fully faithful from k-linear Σ-exact functors P. → B (commuting with Σ-means) to B^·, the cochain complexes in B. Its essential image consists of the complexes whose differentials admit Σ-means. On this page that subcategory is called B^·_{Σ-sex}.
- (b) Its essential image on Σ-exact functors consists of the Σ-resolutions (Σ-special, acyclic in the appropriate degrees). This is called B^·_{Σ-ex}.
- Read this way, (P., C^·., Σ.) is the universal triple (B, C^·, Σ) carrying a Σ-resolution. It is a universal property of finite free complexes as the free Σ-exact k-linear category on one acyclic complex.

Indications of proof on this page:

1. Let Ψ^i. = k placed in degree i. Each C^i. is a 'disk' (k in two adjacent degrees, identity differential). It sits in a degreewise split sequence 0 → Ψ^i. → C^i. → Ψ^{i+1}. → 0. Splicing these gives 0 → Ψ^0. → C^0. → C^1. → …, so C^·. is a Σ.-resolution of Ψ^0. inside P.

2. Dévissage. Every L. in P. carries the stupid (bête) filtration Fil_i(L.)_j = L_j for j ≤ i and 0 for j > i. Its graded pieces are Gr_i(L.) ≅ L_i[i] ≅ Ψ^i. ⊗_k L_i canonically, and ≅ (Ψ^i.)^{β_i} non-canonically, with β_i = rank L_i. So every object is an iterated Σ-extension of sums of the Ψ^i.

3. The C^i. are Σ-projective. Hom(disk, X) is a component X_j, so Hom(C^i., −) sends degreewise split epimorphisms to surjections.

4. Strategy: build quasi-inverse functors B^·_{Σ-sex} → Hom_{Σ-sex}(P., B) and B^·_{Σ-ex} → Hom_{Σ-ex}(P., B), the first inducing the second. The next page does this via σ(C^·)(L.) = Hom^·_k(Ľ., C^·), using the adjunction Hom(F(C^·.), C^·) ≅ Hom(F, σ(C^·)).

The whole thing is groundwork for the dévissage of ∂-perfect half-simplicial complexes. Presumably it reduces the construction of multiplicative or determinant-type structures to the generators Ψ^i and C^i.
errors: Nothing wrong in substance. The page is only a proof sketch: the key step (existence and Σ-exactness of the extension functor, i.e. that σ(C^·)(L.) is well defined using Σ-kernels/means) is postponed to the next page.

The next page itself raises a doubt ('Non, il faut condition de platitude ?'). That suggests the statement as formulated on the previous page may need an extra flatness or exactness hypothesis on B or Σ.

ideas.what: Stupid filtration of a bounded complex, with graded pieces L_i[i] ≅ (k[i])^{rank}; dévissage of perfect complexes into shifted free modules
ideas.modern_name: brutal/stupid filtration σ_{≤i}; weight-structure style dévissage
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard (Deligne, Hodge II; SGA 6 style dévissage)
ideas.where_published: SGA 6 (Illusie, exposé I) uses such dévissages of perfect complexes

ideas.what: Disk complexes are projective for the degreewise split exact structure; Ψ^i → C^i → Ψ^{i+1} sequences
ideas.modern_name: Frobenius exact structure on Ch(A); disks as projective-injectives

ideas.what: Universal property: Σ-exact k-linear functors out of the category of finite free complexes correspond to Σ-resolutions (complexes with Σ-means) in the target, via evaluation on a universal cochain object
ideas.modern_name: free exact/additive category on a complex; Ch^b(proj k) as a universal (Frobenius) category; cf. Keller's description of complexes as modules over a disk category
ideas.usually_credited_to: unsure – related ideas in Keller, and in Barwick/Blumberg–Gepner–Tabuada universal properties

missed.claim: Grothendieck formulates (and sketches a proof of) a universal property: the category of finite free complexes with degreewise split sequences is the universal k-linear category with an exact structure Σ carrying a Σ-resolution (or a complex with Σ-means). This is meant as the base for dévissage of ∂-perfect half-simplicial complexes and multiplicative structures.
missed.quote: B^._{Σ-sex} → Hom_{Σ-sex}(P., B) ; B^._{Σ-ex} → Hom_{Σ-ex}(P., B) (le premier induisant le deuxième)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is an early 1-categorical version of 'free exact category on a complex' universal properties. These are used today in K-theory, for determinant functors, and for universal properties of perfect complexes. It is of mild historical interest; the mathematics itself is accessible to specialists.

deep.surprise_reason: The page contains routine dévissage (stupid filtration, disks projective). The surrounding universal-property statement is a nice unpublished formulation, but close to known folklore about free exact categories and complexes.
transcription_corrections: 'si $-\Psi^i. = ... k placé en degré i'' should read 'si Ψ^i. = k placé en degré i' (the leading dash is a stray mark).
'Dans P., il est évident que C^i. est une Σ. résolution' likely refers to the whole cochain object C^·. (double-struck C), not a single C^i.
'on voit que C^i. ... a des suites ⊂ Σ' is likely 'on voit que C^·. s'obtient en recollant des suites ∈ Σ' (meaning: spliced from Σ-sequences).
The third displayed sequence should read 0 → Ψ^2. → C^2. → Ψ^3. → …
'Σ-sex' presumably abbreviates 'Σ-semi-exact', matching condition a) on Σ-means.
